subject: Procedure division structure
notes: kb/Work PB1010 (2026-09-22): both directions of 'if and only if'. IF: the declaratives format (Format 1) is accepted and runs in a program definition (every declarative golden), a function definition (probe: a FUNCTION-ID's USE AFTER EC EC-SIZE runs), and now a METHOD definition. Before this change a method was refused COBOL0899. A method's declarative sections bind at the head of its pc slice through the same DeclCollectSection a program's take, and its selection machinery is emitted method-local, so a condition raised in a method selects the method's own USE statements (14.9.49.4 GR3/GR4 a)). ONLY IF: an instance, factory or interface definition's own procedure division is the object-oriented format, which holds method definitions only (SR12/SR13); DECLARATIVES written there are a syntax error (COBOL0001). Program and function prototypes are governed by SR11 (a procedure division header only), which is a separate row.
